source.title: DeepNet: Scaling Transformers to 1,000 Layers
source.authors: Hongyu Wang; Shu-Ming Ma; Li Dong; Shao-Han Huang; Dong-Dong Zhang; Furu Wei

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; Appendix E tables are heavily garbled, but the main results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Reports depth and optimization-stability results for Transformer machine translation, extending deep-training findings to a different architecture and task. It does not measure training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation loss, BLEU, and divergence, not training classification error. It compares depth and stabilization methods in Transformers; cited results from other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study uses Xavier initialization, residual connections and Fixup-inspired analysis to develop DeepNorm, then evaluates Transformer translation performance and stability. None of V1–V6 covers these residual, layer-normalized Transformers or their BLEU and validation-loss outcomes. Related optimization results alone do not establish a T3 test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that DeepNorm's residual scaling and initialization stabilize Transformer optimization, enabling 1,000-layer models, with effectiveness demonstrated on machine-translation benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DeepNorm residual normalization and architecture-dependent initialization in Transformers, evaluated on machine-translation tasks. The claim versions focus on classification tasks, other architectures, or other interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Transformer depth, normalization/initialization method, precision, learning rate, batch size, and hidden dimension are varied or reported as affecting outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: At 18L-18L on IWSLT-14, changing initialization while holding the Post-LN Transformer architecture fixed changed failure to converge into convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization can determine convergence in deep residual Transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-LN methods became unstable at 50L-50L on WMT-17; DeepNet remained stable across its IWSLT-14 depth sweep and exceeded 30 BLEU after 8,000 steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformer depth-related stability and translation performance depend on the residual scaling, normalization and initialization recipe.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The relevant stability results concern machine translation and validation loss/BLEU rather than training classification error. Several curves are presented only in figures without tabulated values; the large multilingual comparison also uses baseline results taken directly from the cited paper.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the extracted main-text results. Appendix E contains large, flattened evaluation tables, but they report translation scores rather than training-error outcomes relevant to the claim.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels.
Spurious-minimum frequency and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation in plain convolutional networks versus identity-shortcut networks; deep plain tanh and Fixup residual-network conditions.

Activation-matched initialization in plain networks, including orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization and orthogonal convolution kernels. The initialization comparison here uses residual Transformers.
Recovery or divergence relative to a measured linearized stability threshold, curvature reduction and edge-of-stability dynamics. Larger learning rates alone do not test these effects.

Batch normalization versus no batch normalization, and Fixup residual-network training speed and stability. Layer-normalization comparisons and Transformer Fixup variants do not establish these results.

record.verdict_notes: No supplied version is tested, so no verdict labels are warranted. States are cannot_determine relative to those versions; this does not dispute the reported Transformer outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR training classification error; random or corrupted labels; SGD/Adam outcomes against that measure.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequency, and neuron-width comparisons.
Plain versus shortcut convolutional networks on ImageNet or CIFAR-10; training error; the specified tanh and Fixup conditions.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons in the specified plain networks, including tanh and 10,000-layer convolutional results.
Squared-loss learning-rate stability threshold, catapult recovery, sharpness, or divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch-normalization comparisons on the specified vision datasets and Fixup without normalization.

rows.subject: 18L-18L Post-LN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on IWSLT-14 De-En; paper reports validation-loss convergence behavior.
rows.note: The paper describes the outcome but gives no numeric validation-loss value in the text.
rows.check: The reported convergence comparison is accurate, but it concerns residual Transformers and validation loss. Failure to converge is not an absent effect for any supplied version.

rows.subject: Post-LN baselines

rows.value: Post-LN baselines lead to unstable optimization when depth goes to 50L-50L
rows.note: The text reports the depth-associated instability; it does not give training classification error.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports unstable optimization at 50L-50L, and Table 1 reports divergence for Post-LN methods. Calling this partial is unsupported; it does not measure a supplied version.

rows.value: stable from shallow to deep; performance keeps improving as the model goes deeper
